newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm on Eurobond issue news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm on Eurobond issue news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on news of Russia's bigger than expected Eurobond issue and news more bonds were unfrozen, but dealers said some operators were already taking profits on these developments.
Joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg said earlier on Thursday the $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond will be priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Mikhail Ignatyev, a detective in the investigations department of the 5th central Moscow police precinct, told Reuters he had issued an order to unfreeze $56.81 million of bonds which he had frozen in June.
"Prices rose 0.6-1.00 point on the news about the Eurobond. The released bonds are good news as well but it was already priced in," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
But another dealer said buying was not really frenetic at the moment as a narrower spread over Treasuries for the Eurobond had been expected.
"The total amount of issue is good but the spread could have been better. Somebody is taking profits now," one dealer said.
Dealers said prices could firm further today but aggressive buying was unlikely.
